# Llamatik 2.2.2 Android candidate provenance

The Maven Central `com.llamatik:core-android:2.2.2` AAR was inspected on Cortex on 2026-11-07. It is 83,718,561 bytes with SHA-256 `8fb2020cceb5396917c0363cd5852fb52532a003bc0b9ad51539859acc2a3fc3`, matching its published module metadata and the retained [2.2.0 hash and size record](../llamatik-2.2.0/PROVENANCE.md). Original 2.2.0 bytes were not found in the searched caches, so no direct byte comparison was performed. Matching SHA-256 supports identical binary content. Version and publication metadata differ. The candidate POM declares MIT; its POM and module metadata are retained here.

The archive contains four ABIs: `arm64-v8a`, `armeabi-v7a`, `x86`, and `x86_64`. Each includes ggml-base, ggml, llama-common, llama, llama_jni, omp, parakeet, whisper and ggml-cpu libraries. ARM64 has seven architecture-specific ggml-cpu variants; other ABIs have one each. No archive entry named license or notice was found. Existing retained notices and their packaging remain required.

The [publisher follow-up](https://github.com/llamatik/Llamatik/issues/184#issuecomment-6681501282) corrects its earlier account: recursive checkout initialized the codecs and enabled their defaults, but EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL and disabled examples left their targets unlinked. This is publisher attribution, not an independently verified link map or original CMake cache. It resolves the contradictory publisher explanation, without proving every native component's source or notice requirements.

This update corrects the dependency version and MIT publication metadata while preserving the existing binary identity evidence. It establishes no new native permission ambiguity or specific missing codec notice. The retained partial source mapping and native notice completeness limits still apply. It grants no blanket license clearance, artwork permission, distribution approval, iOS qualification or runtime acceptance. Hardware and E2E checks are NOT_RUN and deferred under the current phase.
